A course change proposal will not be necessary if faculty/departments teaching a class in one of the three ‘online only’ modalities (‘Online synchronous’, ‘Online synchronous and asynchronous’, ‘Online asynchronous’) wish to adopt (or add, in the case of a multi-section class) another of the ‘online’ modalities.
A major course change proposal is necessary for courses with one of the three ‘in-person’ modalities that wish to adopt (or add, in the case of a multi-section class) one of the three ‘online only’ modalities. This is also true for ‘online only’ modality courses that wish to adopt/add an ‘in-person’ modality.”
C. New Courses: New Course proposals follow the review/approval process described under “Major Change” above.” #2025-2026-FSEC-01
Student Learning Outcomes Assessment & Accreditation – Office for the Advancement of Teaching and Learning

The Student Learning Outcomes Assessment and Accreditation (SLOAA) team promotes student success, improved learning, and continuous program improvement through program-level outcomes assessment and curricular innovation.
We support URI’s commitment to evidence-informed assessment, reflection, and continuous improvement processes that enhance student achievement through collaboration, education, and outreach.

Beginning with the 2026-2027 academic year , all undergraduate academic programs will participate in a three-year academic program assessment cycle .
Department chairs for programs in the May 2027 assessment cohort will be invited to meet with our office during September 2026 .
Department chairs for programs in the May 2028 assessment cohort will be invited to meet with our office during October 2026 .

The cycle includes all undergraduate programs previously supported through our assessment process, as well as newly established and revised academic programs identified during the review and planning process.
